title: Decay of a Gaussian density expression
statement: Let $\varphi(x)$ be the standard Gaussian density, and define $F(x)=\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$, with reciprocals interpreted as zero when their denominator is zero. Then $F(x)$ tends to $0$ as $x$ tends to $-\infty$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, and define $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by $F(0)=0$ and $F(x)=\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$ for $x\ne0$. Its limit at negative infinity is $\lim_{x\to-\infty}F(x)=0$.
